questions.prompt: Describe two skills from an invasion game of your choice, giving key technique points for each.
questions.model: Activity: Gaelic football. Skill one, kicking from the hands: the player keeps their eyes on the ball, places the non-kicking foot beside the line of the ball, and strikes through it, following through towards the target, so the kick has accuracy and direction. Skill two, the hand pass: the ball is held in one hand and struck with the fist or open palm rather than thrown, so the pass can be delivered quickly to a team-mate in a tight space, without losing control of the ball.

questions.prompt: Describe the lay-up in basketball and explain how a coach could use part practice to teach it.
questions.model: Lay-up: a right-hand lay-up is taken off the left foot after two steps. The player gathers the ball, takes two steps towards the basket, jumps off the left foot and places the ball up towards the basket with the right hand. Part practice: the coach isolates one sub-routine of the lay-up and practises it alone before the whole skill. First the footwork, two steps and a jump off the left foot, is practised without the ball. Next the ball handling is added, with a gather and a catch while stepping. Then the release is practised on its own, placing the ball up with the right hand. When each part is secure, the coach puts them back together and the player performs the whole lay-up.
